title: How to Make Any Cupcake Recipe Vegan
summaryShort: To make cupcakes vegan, swap each egg for a matching substitute, use block plant butter, replace milk with plant milk, and switch to a plant butter frosting. Pick the egg swap by batter type, then test one small batch.
metaTitle: How to Make Any Cupcake Recipe Vegan
metaDescription: Learn how to make cupcakes vegan with swaps for eggs, butter, milk and frosting, plus a worked vanilla example. Convert your favorite recipe today.
sidebarBullets: Light batter: 3 tbsp aquafaba or 1/4 cup plant yogurt per egg
Dense or spiced batter: 1/4 cup applesauce or 1 flax egg per egg
Butter: use block plant butter, not tub spread.
Buttermilk: 1 cup plant milk plus 1 tbsp vinegar.
Make all the swaps, then bake 2 test cupcakes first.

sections.heading: Start With a Simple Conversion Plan
paragraphs: The easiest way to make cupcakes vegan is to change four things in order: eggs, butter, milk, and frosting. Each one has a job in the batter, so you match the swap to the job.
In my kitchen, changing everything at once works fine as long as you pick the right swaps up front.
list: Eggs: pick a swap based on how light the batter is.
Butter: use a firm plant butter block.
Milk: use unsweetened plant milk, with vinegar if the recipe wants buttermilk.
Frosting: swap butter and cream for plant butter and plant milk.
Check the sugar too, since a few brands filter it with bone char.

sections.heading: Choose the Right Egg Swap for Your Batter
paragraphs: Aquafaba suits light vanilla and lemon batters, while flax and applesauce suit dense, spiced, or chocolate batters. Eggs bind, add moisture, and trap air, and no single swap does all three well.
Use the chart above for quick picks. For full measurements and more options, see my egg substitutes guide.
list: Aquafaba: 3 tbsp per egg, best for white and yellow cakes.
Plant yogurt: 1/4 cup per egg, best for tender, moist crumb
Applesauce: 1/4 cup per egg, best for banana, carrot, and spice
Flax egg: 1 tbsp ground flax plus 3 tbsp water per egg, best for chocolate and oat batters.

sections.heading: Swap Butter and Milk Without Losing Texture
paragraphs: Use block plant butter one to one for dairy butter, and unsweetened plant milk one to one for milk. Tub spreads hold extra water, so they make greasy, flat cupcakes.
Oil also works and often gives a moister crumb. Use about 3/4 cup oil for every 1 cup butter, and read my butter vs oil guide for the trade-offs.
list: Buttermilk swap: 1 cup plant milk plus 1 tbsp white vinegar or lemon juice.
Let it sit 5 minutes until it looks slightly curdled.
Soy and oat milk curdle best, almond works too.
Choose unsweetened and unflavored so the vanilla still tastes like vanilla.

sections.heading: Frosting Without Dairy
paragraphs: Vegan buttercream works with block plant butter, powdered sugar, a splash of plant milk, and vanilla. Beat the butter for a full 3 minutes before adding sugar so it turns pale and fluffy.
Plant butter softens faster than dairy butter, so keep frosted cupcakes cool. If it turns soft, chill the bowl for 15 minutes and whip again. My frosting fix guide covers runny batches.

sections.heading: What Fails When You Convert
paragraphs: The most common failures are gummy centers, sunken tops, and flat, greasy cupcakes. Each one points to a specific swap that did not suit the batter.
Recipes built on four or more eggs, like sponge or angel food style cakes, rarely convert well. Stick to butter-cake style recipes with one to three eggs.
list: Gummy middle: too much flax or applesauce, so cut back or switch to yogurt.
Sunken top: aquafaba was under-whipped or the batter sat too long before baking.
Greasy and flat: tub spread used instead of block butter.
Dense crumb: batter overmixed after adding plant milk.
Pale tops: add 1 tsp extra sugar or bake 2 minutes longer.

sections.heading: Worked Example: Classic Vanilla Cupcakes
paragraphs: Here is a standard vanilla recipe converted: 1 1/2 cups flour, 3/4 cup sugar, 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 cup butter, 2 eggs, 1/2 cup milk, and 2 tsp vanilla. I used 1/2 cup block plant butter, 6 tbsp aquafaba, and 1/2 cup soy milk with 1 tsp vinegar.
Cream the butter and sugar, whip the aquafaba until foamy, then mix in the milk and vanilla. Fold in the flour just until smooth and bake at 350°F for 18 to 20 minutes.
list: Butter: 1/2 cup block plant butter, softened
Eggs: 6 tbsp aquafaba, whipped to soft foam.
Milk: 1/2 cup soy milk plus 1 tsp white vinegar
What to expect: tall, tender, and pale gold, with a light crumb.

howToSteps: Check the recipe for eggs, butter, milk, and cream, and note the amounts.
Pick an egg swap that matches the batter type using the chart.
Replace butter with block plant butter, or use 3/4 the amount of neutral oil.
Swap milk for unsweetened plant milk and add 1 tbsp vinegar per cup if it needs buttermilk.
Mix the batter gently and fill liners two-thirds full.
Bake 2 test cupcakes first and check them at 16 minutes.
Make frosting with block plant butter, powdered sugar, and a little plant milk.

faq.question: Which egg replacer is best for vanilla cupcakes?
faq.answer: Aquafaba is my top pick for vanilla because it adds lift and has no flavor. Use 3 tablespoons per egg and whip it to soft foam first.

faq.question: Can I use tub vegan butter in cupcakes?
faq.answer: It is risky. Tub spreads contain more water, which can make cupcakes greasy and flat. Block plant butter behaves much closer to dairy butter.

faq.question: Does plant milk plus vinegar really work as buttermilk?
faq.answer: Yes, for baking. The acid thickens soy or oat milk and activates baking soda, giving a tender crumb. Wait 5 minutes before using it.

faq.question: Why did my vegan cupcakes turn out gummy?
faq.answer: Too much moisture from flax or applesauce is the usual cause. Switch to plant yogurt or aquafaba, or use one less egg replacement.

faq.question: Can I convert a recipe that uses four or more eggs?
faq.answer: It is hard to do well. Look for a butter-cake recipe with one to three eggs, or start from one of my vegan cupcake recipes.
